Love of Allah, His Messenger, and His pious servants entails doing what He loves and abandoning what He dislikes. People differ enormously in this regard: the greater a person’s share of this, the higher his rank with Allah.

As for someone who loves another out of personal desire—for some worldly benefit he receives from him, some need that person meets for him, money he obtains through him, partisan attachment to him, or similar reasons—this is not love for Allah’s sake. Rather, it is love driven by personal desire. This is the love that leads those who harbour it into disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience.

How many people claim to love shaykhs for Allah’s sake! Had they truly loved them for Allah’s sake, they would have obeyed Allah, for whose sake they loved them. Love for someone who is loved for another’s sake is subordinate to love for that other. How can someone who does not love Allah love anyone for Allah’s sake? And how can someone who turns away from the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—and from Allah’s path be someone who loves Allah?

How many people love shaykhs, kings, and others, taking them as rivals to Allah and loving them as they love Allah! The distinction between loving for Allah’s sake and loving alongside Allah is clear. Those who associate partners with Allah take rivals whom they love as they love Allah, whereas the believers are stronger in their love for Allah.

The people of faith love, for the foundation of their love is love of Allah. Whoever loves Allah loves those whom Allah loves, and whoever is loved by Allah loves Allah. Thus, the beloved of the beloved is beloved to Allah and loves Allah. Whoever loves Allah is loved by Allah, and therefore loves those who love Allah.

As for those who associate partners with Allah, they take rivals and intercessors whom they invoke besides Allah. Allah Most High says:

“You have come to Us alone, just as We created you the first time, leaving behind all that We bestowed upon you. We do not see with you those intercessors whom you claimed to be Allah’s partners in your affairs. The bonds between you have been severed, and all that you claimed has vanished from you.”

Allah Most High also says:

“Why should I not worship the One who created me, and to whom you will be returned?”

“Should I take other gods besides Him? If the Most Merciful intends harm for me, their intercession will avail me nothing, nor can they rescue me.”

“Then I would surely be in manifest error.”

“Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me.”

Allah Most High says:

“Warn with it those who fear being gathered before their Lord, with no protector or intercessor besides Him, so that they may become mindful of Him.”

Allah Most High also says:

“It is not for any human being to whom Allah has given the Scripture, judgment, and prophethood to then say to people, ‘Be my worshippers instead of Allah’s.’ Rather, ‘Be devoted to the Lord through your teaching of the Scripture and through your study of it.’”

“Nor would he command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords. Would he command you to disbelieve after you have submitted to Allah?”

Allah Most High sent the messengers and revealed the Scriptures so that all worship would be devoted to Allah alone. The Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said in an authentic hadith:

“We prophets share one religion.”

Thus, the religion is one, even though the prescribed laws and ways differ. Allah Most High says:

“We never sent a messenger before you without revealing to him: ‘There is no god but Me, so worship Me.’”

Allah Most High also says:

“Ask those of Our messengers whom We sent before you: Did We appoint gods besides the Most Merciful to be worshipped?”

Allah Most High says: “We certainly sent a messenger to every nation

saying, ‘Worship Allah and shun false gods.’”

Ever since Allah sent Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—He accepts from anyone whom the message has reached only the religion with which He sent him, for his call extends to all creation. Allah Most High says:

“We have sent you only to all humanity.”

The Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said:

“Any Jew or Christian of this community who hears of me and then does not believe in me will enter the Fire.”

Allah Most High says:

“My mercy encompasses all things. I shall ordain it for those who are mindful of Me, give zakat, and believe in Our signs.”

“Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find described in the Torah and the Gospel they possess. He enjoins upon them what is right and forbids them what is wrong, makes good things lawful for them and forbids them foul things, and relieves them of their burdens and the shackles that bound them. Those who believe in him, honour him, support him, and follow the light sent down with him—it is they who will prosper.”

“Say, ‘O humanity! I am Allah’s Messenger to you all. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. There is no god but Him; He gives life and causes death. So believe in Allah and His Messenger, the unlettered Prophet who believes in Allah and His words, and follow him so that you may be guided.’”

All creation must therefore follow Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—worshipping none but Allah and worshipping Him according to the law of Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—and no other. Allah Most High says:

“Then We set you upon a clear path in matters of religion, so follow it, and do not follow the desires of those who do not know.”

“They will be of no help to you against Allah. Indeed, some of the wrongdoers

are allies of one another, while Allah is the ally of those mindful of Him.”

They must unite upon this and not divide, as is established in an authentic report from the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—who said:

“Allah is pleased with three things for you: that you worship Him without associating anything with Him; that you all hold firmly to the rope of Allah and do not divide; and that you offer sincere counsel to those whom Allah has placed in charge of your affairs.”

Worship of Allah entails complete love for Allah and complete humility before Him. The foundation and basis of religion is that Allah alone should be the One worshipped, whom hearts love and fear, and that they should have no deity besides Him. A “deity” is that which hearts worship with love, reverence, hope, fear, veneration, exaltation, and the like.

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, sent the messengers with the message that there is no deity but Him. Thus, through love for Him and hope in Him, hearts are freed from love for anything besides Him; through asking Him, from asking anything besides Him; through acting for Him, from acting for anything besides Him; and through seeking His help, from seeking help from anything besides Him. This is why the middle of al-Fātihah is:

“You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.”

The Prophet—may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace—said in an authentic hadith that Allah Most High says:

“I have divided the prayer between Myself and My servant. When he says, ‘The Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful,’ He says, ‘My servant has extolled Me.’ When he says, ‘Master of the Day of Judgment,’ He says, ‘My servant has glorified Me.’ When he says, ‘You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help,’ He says, ‘This verse is divided into two halves between Myself and My servant, and My servant shall have what he asks for.’ And when he says, ‘Guide us to the straight path’

‘the path of those You have blessed, not those who have incurred Your wrath, nor those who have gone astray,’ He says, ‘These are for My servant, and My servant shall have what he asks for.’”

Thus, the middle of the surah is:

“You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.”

Religion, then, consists in worshipping Allah alone and seeking help from Him alone. The angels, the prophets, and all others are servants of Allah. As Allah Most High says:

“The Messiah would never disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor would the angels brought near to Him. Whoever disdains to worship Him and is arrogant—He will gather them all before Him.

“As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full and grant them more from His bounty. But those who are disdainful and arrogant, He will punish with a painful punishment, and they will find neither protector nor helper besides Allah.”

Love for other than Allah is exemplified by the Christians’ love for the Messiah, the Jews’ love for Moses, the Rāfidah’s love for ‘Alī, and the extremists’ love for their shaykhs and imams. An example is someone who gives his allegiance to a shaykh or imam and turns others away from his counterpart, although the two are close or equal in rank. This is akin to the conduct of the People of the Book who believed in some messengers and disbelieved in others; to that of the Rāfidah, who give their allegiance to some Companions and show hostility towards others; and to that of partisans among those associated with jurisprudence and asceticism, who give their allegiance to some shaykhs and imams but not others. The true believer, however, is one who gives his allegiance to all people of faith.

Allah Most High says:

“The believers are but brothers.”

The Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said:

“One believer is to another like a building, each part strengthening the other”—and he interlaced his fingers.

And he said: “The likeness of

believers in their mutual love and compassion is that of a body: when one part suffers, the rest of the body responds with fever and sleeplessness.” He—peace be upon him—also said:

“Do not sever ties with one another or turn your backs on one another. Be brothers, O servants of Allah.”

The distinction between love for Allah’s sake and love for other motives is further illustrated by Abū Bakr—may Allah be pleased with him—who loved the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—with sincere devotion to Allah. His uncle Abū Tālib, however, loved and supported him out of personal inclination, not for Allah’s sake. Allah therefore accepted Abū Bakr’s deeds and revealed concerning him:

“But the most God-fearing will be kept away from it—he who gives his wealth to purify himself, not to repay anyone for a favor done to him, but seeking the Face of his Lord, the Most High. And he will surely be pleased.”

As for Abū Tālib, Allah did not accept his deeds. Abū Bakr sought neither recompense nor reward from any created being—not from the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—nor from anyone else. Rather, he believed in him, loved him, protected him, and supported him with his person and his wealth, seeking thereby to draw near to Allah and seeking reward from Allah. His Messenger conveys Allah’s commands and prohibitions, His promise and His warning. Allah Most High says:

“Your duty is only to convey the message, and Ours is to call to account.”

Allah alone creates and provides, gives and withholds, lowers and raises, grants honor and brings humiliation. He—glory be to Him—is the One who brings all causes into being, the Lord and Sovereign of everything. Among the means that people employ are those Allah has commanded or permitted; these may be pursued. Others He has prohibited outright, or they are religious innovations for which Allah has given no permission; these must not be pursued. Allah Most High says:

“Say, ‘Call upon those whom you claim

translated_text:
besides Allah.’ They do not possess even an atom’s weight in the heavens or on earth, nor do they have any share in either, nor does He have any helper among them.”

“Intercession is of no avail with Him except for those to whom He grants permission.”

He—glory be to Him—has explained the error of those who invoke created beings, whether angels, prophets, or others. He made clear that created beings do not possess even an atom’s weight in the heavens or on earth; then He made clear that they have no share in either; then He made clear that He has no helper or supporter among them.

For those who associate partners with Allah liken the Creator to created beings. Some of them say: “If you have a need, call upon Shaykh so-and-so, and you will find him; or take steps toward his tomb and call out, ‘O Shaykh!’ Your need will be fulfilled.” This is an error, and doing so is impermissible. Even if some of those who invoke others besides Allah occasionally see the likeness of the one they invoke, that is a devil appearing to them in his likeness. Such things have happened to many people. Similar to this is the statement of some ignorant followers of Shaykh ‘Adī and others: “Any provision that does not come through the shaykh’s hands, I do not want.”

It is astonishing that anyone of sound mind should call upon someone who is dead and seek his aid—yet not seek the aid of the Ever-Living, who never dies!

One of them says: “If you need something from a king, you seek access to him through his aides; likewise, one seeks access to Him through the shaykhs.” These are the words of people of polytheism and misguidance. A king does not know the needs of his subjects, nor can he meet them on his own, nor does he wish to do so except for some benefit that will accrue

to him as a result. But Allah has full knowledge of all things: He knows what is secret and what is even more hidden, and He has power over all things. All causes originate with Him and return to Him. Every cause is dependent upon other causes and subject to counteracting factors. Fire, for example, burns only what is susceptible to burning; it does not burn the salamander. When Allah wills, He prevents its effect, as He did for Abraham, peace be upon him.

The Lord’s will, however, depends on no one else, and nothing can prevent it. Whatever Allah wills happens, and whatever He does not will does not happen. He—glory be to Him—is more merciful to His servants than a mother is to her child. He treats them kindly, has mercy upon them, and relieves their suffering, although He has no need of them and they are utterly dependent upon Him.

“There is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.”

The Lord thus ruled out all these possibilities, leaving only intercession. He said:

“Intercession is of no avail with Him except for those to whom He grants permission.”

And He said:

“Who is there who can intercede with Him except by His permission?”

He is the One who permits intercession, and He is the One who accepts it; it all comes from Him alone. The more sincerely a person devotes himself to Allah, the more likely he is to receive the Messenger’s intercession.

Abū Hurayrah said to him: “Who will be most fortunate in receiving your intercession, O Messenger of Allah?”

He replied: “Whoever says, ‘There is no deity worthy of worship but Allah,’ seeking thereby the Face of Allah.”

As for those who place their trust in someone to intercede for them apart from Allah Most High, and attach themselves to that person, they are like the polytheists who have taken intercessors besides

Allah Most High. Allah Most High says:

“Or have they taken intercessors besides Allah? Say, ‘Even though they possess nothing and have no understanding?’”

“Say, ‘All intercession belongs to Allah.’”

Allah Most High also says:

“Then He rose above the Throne. You have no protector or intercessor besides Him.”

And He says:

“Say, ‘Call upon those whom you claim to be gods besides Him. They have no power to remove your suffering or to shift it elsewhere.’”

“Those whom they invoke themselves seek a means of drawing near to their Lord, vying to be nearest to Him. They hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. Indeed, your Lord’s punishment is ever to be feared.”

A group of the early generations said that some people used to invoke the Messiah, Ezra, and the angels. Allah Most High therefore explained that these prophets and angels are His servants, just as those who invoke them are His servants. They draw near to Allah, hope for His mercy, and fear His punishment.

The polytheists have taken rivals alongside Allah, loving them as they love Allah, and have taken intercessors to intercede for them with Allah. They thus love these beings and associate them with Allah. Their conduct resembles that of the Christians in their love for the Messiah and their association of him with Allah.

The believers, however, are stronger in their love for Allah. They worship Allah alone and do not set up anything alongside Him that they love as they love Him—neither His prophets nor anyone else. Rather, out of their love for Allah, they love what He loves. They devote their religion sincerely to Allah and know that no one can intercede for them except by His permission. Thus, they love Allah’s servant and Messenger Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, out of their love for Allah. They know that he is Allah’s servant who conveys His message, so they obey his commands and believe what he reports. They place their hope in Allah alone, fear Allah alone, and ask Allah alone. His intercession for those for whom

he intercedes is by Allah’s permission. Neither our hope in the intercessor nor our fear of him benefits us. What benefits us is worshipping Allah alone, being sincere to Him, and placing our trust in Him, for He is the One who grants the intercessor permission. A Muslim must therefore distinguish his love and religion from those of the Christians and polytheists, follow the people of monotheism and faith, and cease resembling the polytheists and worshippers of crosses.

It is reported in the two Sahīh collections that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever possesses three qualities will taste the sweetness of faith: that Allah and His Messenger are dearer to him than all else; that he loves a person solely for Allah’s sake; and that he hates to return to disbelief after Allah has saved him from it as much as he hates to be thrown into the Fire.”

“Say, ‘If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your relatives, the wealth you have acquired, the trade whose decline you fear, and the homes you cherish are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His cause, then wait until Allah brings about His command. Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.’”

Allah Most High says:

“Whoever among you turns away from his religion—Allah will bring forth a people whom He loves and who love Him, humble toward the believers and firm toward the disbelievers, striving in Allah’s cause and fearing no one’s reproach. That is Allah’s bounty, which He grants to whom He wills. Allah is All-Bountiful, All-Knowing.”

This is a vast subject. The religion of Islam is built upon this foundation, and the Quran revolves around it.

He—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked about “humility” and the Prophet’s words, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“O Allah, let me live in humility and die in humility, and gather me among the humble.”

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. This hadith was narrated by al-Tirmidhī, and Abū al-Faraj mentioned it in al-Mawdū‘āt (Fabricated Reports). Whether or not its wording is authentic, the humble person who deserves praise is one who is modest and submissive before Allah. Humility does not mean lacking wealth. Indeed, a man may be poor yet tyrannical, as the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said in an authentic hadith:

“There are three to whom Allah will not speak, nor will He look at them on the Day of Resurrection or purify them, and theirs will be a painful punishment: a lying king, an arrogant poor man, and an elderly adulterer.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to say:

“I am a servant: I eat as a servant eats and sit as a servant sits.”

Humility is therefore an inward quality: modesty, submissiveness, and gentleness—the opposite of arrogance. As Jesus, peace be upon him, said:

“And dutiful to my mother, and He has not made me a wretched tyrant.”

The poet’s words likewise illustrate this:

“Lowly are those who love; even their graves
Bear the dust of abasement among the tombs.”

That is, they are humble and submissive, for love brings submission. Worship of Allah combines perfect love for Him with perfect submission to Him. Whoever loves something without submitting to it is not its worshipper; nor is someone who submits to it while hating it.

Love has degrees. The highest is tatayyum (enslavement by love), which is worshipful devotion. The expression tayyama Allāha means “he worshipped Allah.” Allah Most High says:

“The servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth humbly, and when the ignorant address them, they say, ‘Peace.’”

And likewise in the verses that follow. The evidence supporting this principle is abundant.

Shaykh al-Islām also said:

Section

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, linked restraint with self-sufficiency in several hadiths. Among them is his statement in the hadith of Abū Sa‘īd recorded in the two Sahīhs:

“Whoever seeks self-sufficiency, Allah will make him self-sufficient; and whoever seeks to refrain from begging, Allah will enable him to refrain.”

Another is his statement in the hadith of ‘Iyād ibn Himār in Sahīh Muslim:

“The people of Paradise are of three kinds: a just ruler, and a self-sufficient man who exercises restraint and gives charity.”

Another is his statement in the hadith about horses recorded in the Sahīh:

“And a man who keeps them to secure his livelihood and avoid begging, without forgetting Allah’s due concerning their necks and backs: they are a protection for him.”

Another is the report narrated from him:

“Whoever seeks wealth to be independent of others and refrain from begging will meet Allah with his face like the moon on the night when it is full.”

Another is his statement in the hadith of ‘Umar and others:

“Whatever comes to you of this wealth without your asking for it or eagerly desiring it, accept it.”

The one who asks does so with his tongue, unlike the one who refrains from begging. The one who eagerly desires does so in his heart, and this is contrary to self-sufficiency.

He said concerning the poor:

“Those unaware of their condition think them wealthy because of their restraint.”

He also said:

A self-sufficient soul does not look longingly to created beings. A free man is a slave as long as he covets, and a slave is free as long as he is content.

Shaykh al-Islām said:

Section

It is reported in a hadith:

“The greatest major sins are disbelief and arrogance.”

This is true, for these two sins underlie every sin committed by humans and jinn. Iblīs was the first to commit them, and he is their source.

Allah Most High said:

“Except Iblīs, who refused and was arrogant, and became one of the disbelievers.”

And He said:

“Except Iblīs, who was arrogant and became one of the disbelievers.”

In Sahīh Muslim, Ibn Masʿūd reported that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“No one with an atom’s weight of faith in his heart will enter the Fire, and no one with an atom’s weight of arrogance in his heart will enter Paradise.”

He thus made arrogance the opposite of faith. The same applies to associating partners with Allah, as in His words:

“Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him.”

Ibn Masʿūd said that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“Whoever dies without associating anything with Allah will enter Paradise.”

He added: “And I say: Whoever dies while associating anything with Allah will enter the Fire.”

Some people combine both, while others exhibit only one of them. The righteous believer is one whom Allah has spared both. For a person either submits to Allah alone, submits to others alongside Him, or submits neither to Allah nor to anyone else. The first is a believer, the second one who associates partners with Allah, and the third an arrogant disbeliever—though in some cases he may not be a disbeliever. The Christians’ affliction is associating partners with Allah, while the Jews’ affliction is arrogance. As Allah Most High said concerning the Christians:

“They have taken their rabbis and monks as lords besides Allah, and also the Messiah, son of Mary, though they were commanded only to worship one God. There is no deity except Him. Exalted is He above whatever they associate with Him.”

And He said concerning the Jews:

“I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant upon the earth without right.”

For this reason, the Jews were punished by having humiliation and poverty imposed upon them, and the Christians with misguidance, religious innovations, and ignorance.

And Shaykh al-Islām said:

A further point concerning the three things that bring ruin and those that bring salvation—regarding which he mentioned that, when faced with the things that bring ruin, one should attend to one’s own affairs—is his saying:

“Avarice that is obeyed and desire that is followed.”

He thus described the former as being obeyed and the latter as being followed. This—and Allah knows best—is because desire is the soul’s love and craving for something, whether the word denotes the desire itself or the object desired.

A person governed by desire is commanded and summoned by his desire, so he follows it, just as the movements of the limbs follow the heart’s will. Hence Allah Most High said:

“Do not follow the desires of a people who went astray before and led many others astray.”

And He said:

“Who is more astray than one who follows his own desire without guidance from Allah?”

This encompasses following desires in religion, as with the Christians and those who introduce innovations concerning doctrine and divine decree. Thus the early generations used to call them “people of desires,” including the Rāfidah and the Khawārij. Such desire is found among many of the fuqarā and jurists, except those whom Allah protects.

translated_text:
Our fellow scholars have differed over whether jurists who disagree fall under the designation “people of desires,” holding two views on the matter. Judge Abū Ya‘lā included them in this classification, as did Shaykh Abū Hāmid al-Isfarāyīnī, I believe, whereas Ibn ‘Aqīl rejected this.

As for “avarice that is obeyed,” we have mentioned that its harm consists in withholding good. Such withholding is not, in itself, something one loves; rather, one is driven to it by an avid attachment to whatever one is unwilling to part with. It belongs to the realm of aversion and hatred: it commands a person, and he obeys it. Not everyone who is obeyed is followed, although everyone who is followed is obeyed. A person obeys a physician, a ruler, and others in particular matters without being their follower. Following someone, however, entails obedience and more: the follower goes with him wherever he goes.

A second distinction is that what is followed is sought for its own sake: the follower’s ultimate aim is to attain and obtain it. Such is the nature of desire. What is obeyed, by contrast, serves another end. Such is the nature of avarice.

The precise meaning of avarice is an intense disposition within the soul to withhold. Thus, one may say that someone jealously guards his religion and is unwilling to relinquish it. Avarice is therefore a disposition of the soul, of which miserliness is one manifestation.

Thus, in the two Sahīh collections, Abū Hurayrah reports that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Beware of avarice, for avarice destroyed those before you. It commanded them to be miserly, and they were miserly; it commanded them to commit injustice, and they committed injustice; and it commanded them to sever ties of kinship, and they severed them.”

He was told: “How often you seek refuge from that!” He replied: “If I am protected from the avarice of my own soul, I am protected from injustice, miserliness, and severing ties of kinship”—or words to that effect.

Thus, the Quran and Sunnah explain that avarice and envy belong to the same category, as in His words:

“And they feel no resentment in their hearts over what others have been given, and give them preference over themselves, even though they are in need. And whoever is protected from the avarice of his own soul—it is they who are successful.”

He describes them as giving of the good things they possess despite their own need, and as not resenting the blessings bestowed upon their brothers. The opposite of the first quality is miserliness, and the opposite of the second is envy.

Miserliness and envy therefore belong to the same category: the envious person resents what others are given, while the miser dislikes giving. Then He says:

“And whoever is protected from the avarice of his own soul—it is they who are successful.”

Avarice is the root of both miserliness and envy. It is a narrowness of soul, an unwillingness to wish good for others and an aversion to their receiving it. This gives rise to withholding benefit, which is miserliness, and harming the person who has been blessed, which is injustice. When directed toward relatives, it constitutes severing ties of kinship.

Al-Nasā’ī also narrated it through Jarīr, from Suhayl, from Safwān ibn Abī Yazīd, from al-Qa‘qā‘ ibn al-Lajlāj (*), from Abū Hurayrah, who reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

Consider how he mentioned avarice in the well-known narrations and envy in the other—the former wording being more comprehensive—and how he linked generosity and courage in the hadith. Likewise, he said in another hadith:

“The worst qualities in a person are avarice that torments him and cowardice that robs him of his nerve.”

Thus, he praised courage in Allah’s cause and condemned avarice. Similar to this is his saying:

“There is a kind of proud bearing that Allah loves: a man’s proud bearing in battle and when giving charity.”

The point intended by citing the hadith is His statement:

“And whoever is protected from the avarice of his own soul—it is they who are successful.”

He thus confines success to those protected from the avarice of their own souls. The avaricious person is one who does not like doing good, harms himself, and resents the blessings bestowed on others.

translated_text:
He was asked about certain hadiths: Are they authentic? Has any recognized authority narrated them with an authentic chain of transmission? They are the following sayings attributed to the Prophet:

“When Allah first created the intellect, He said to it, ‘Come forward,’ and it came forward. Then He said to it, ‘Go back,’ and it went back. Then He said, ‘By My might and majesty, I have created nothing more honored by Me than you. Through you I take, and through you I give; through you I reward, and through you I punish.’”

And his saying:

“I have been commanded to address people according to their understanding.”

Is this the actual wording of a hadith, or has it been altered, added to, or shortened?

And his saying:

“Among the favors Allah has bestowed upon me is this: ‘I have given you the Opening of the Book. It is from the treasures of My Throne, and I have divided it into two halves between Me and you.’”

And his saying:

“People share in three things: water, pasture, and fire.”

He answered:

As for the first hadith, it is a fabricated lie according to the scholars of hadith. It is not found in any of the authoritative books of Islam. It is narrated only by the likes of Dāwūd ibn al-Muhabbir and others who have written on the intellect. It is mentioned by the authors of the Epistles of the Brethren of Purity and other such philosophical speculators. Abū Hāmid also mentioned it in some of

his books, as did Ibn ʿArabī, Ibn Sabʿīn, and others like them. Among scholars of hadith, it is regarded as a lie attributed to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as stated by Abū Hātim al-Rāzī, Abū al-Faraj Ibn al-Jawzī, and other authors on the science of hadith.

Nevertheless, the wording of the hadith is:

“When Allah first created the intellect, He said to it, ‘Come forward,’ and it came forward. He said to it, ‘Go back,’ and it went back. He said, ‘I have created nothing more honored by Me than you. Through you I take, and through you I give; through you I reward, and through you I punish.’”

Another version reads:

“When Allah created the intellect, He said the same to it.”

This wording means that He addressed the intellect at the very beginning of its creation. It does not state that the intellect was the first created thing. However, the philosophers who maintain the eternity of the world—the followers of Aristotle, together with those who followed their path among the esoteric Shiites, Sufis, and speculative theologians—narrated it as, “The first thing Allah created was the intellect,” with “the intellect” bearing the nominative ending -u. They did so to support their doctrine that the first thing brought into being is the First Intellect. No scholar of hadith has transmitted it with this wording. Rather, the transmitted wording, despite its weakness, indicates the opposite of this meaning, for He said:

“I have created nothing more honored by Me than you.”

This indicates that He had already created something else before it, whereas, according to the philosophers, nothing was created before what they call the First Intellect.

Furthermore, He said:

“Through you I take, and through you I give; through you I reward, and through you I punish.”

He thus made it the means for these four things, whereas according to those esotericist philosophers:

{أُمِرْت أَنْ أُخَاطِبَ النَّاسَ عَلَى قَدْرِ عُقُولِهِمْ}

translated_text:
the entire universe emanated from the First Intellect, which, according to them, is the lord of the heavens, the earth, and everything between them, although it is itself subject to the lordship of the One whose existence is necessary in Himself. They hold that it is generated from Allah and is a necessary concomitant of His essence. This is not the view of any adherent of the religious communities—Muslims, Jews, or Christians—except those among them who have deviated from their faith. Nor is it the view of the Magians, the majority of the Sabians, most polytheists, or the majority of philosophers. Rather, it is the view of one group among the philosophers.

Furthermore, in Muslim usage, the intellect is an accident inhering in something else: an innate faculty, knowledge, or action based on knowledge. In their usage, the intellect is not a self-subsisting substance. The first created thing therefore cannot be an accident inhering in something else, for an accident can exist only in a substrate; it cannot exist before any concrete entity exists.

Those philosophers, however, define it in their terminology as a self-subsisting substance. This is not what “intellect” means in Muslim usage. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, addressed the Muslims in the language of the Arabs, not that of the Greeks. It is therefore clear that, even if the Messenger had uttered this wording, he would not have intended the meaning meant by these philosophers. How much more so, then, when he did not utter it!

As for the second hadith, namely the saying:

“I have been commanded to address people according to their level of understanding,”

this has not been narrated by any Muslim scholar whose transmission is relied upon, nor is it found in any of their books. The speech with which Allah and His Messenger address people

is general in scope and encompasses all those subject to religious obligations, as in His words:

“O mankind!”

“O you who believe!”

“O My servants!”

“O Children of Israel!”

Likewise, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would address the people from his pulpit with the same words for everyone to hear. Yet people differ in their understanding of those words according to the strength of understanding and soundness of belief that Allah grants each of them.

For this reason, Abū Bakr al-Siddīq understood his intent better than anyone else, as related in the two Sahīh collections on the authority of Abū Sa'īd:

“The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, addressed the people, saying: ‘Allah gave a servant a choice between this world and the Hereafter, and that servant chose what is with Allah.’ Abū Bakr wept and said: ‘We would ransom you with our lives and our wealth!’ The people were astonished at him and said: ‘How astonishing this old man is! He weeps because the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mentioned a servant whom Allah had given a choice between this world and the Hereafter.’ It was the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who had been given the choice, and Abū Bakr understood him better than any of us.”

Thus, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mentioned an unspecified servant without identifying him, but Abū Bakr knew exactly who he was.

As for what some people relate from 'Umar, that he said:

“The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and Abū Bakr would converse, while I was like a man of the Zanj between them,”

this is a fabricated lie. Likewise, the report that he gave Abū Bakr one answer and 'Ā'ishah another is a lie, by the agreement of the scholars.

translated_text:
He was asked about the following hadiths:

“Whoever circumambulates this House seven times, with faith and seeking Allah’s reward, will have his past sins forgiven.”

And the saying attributed to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“Whoever stands at ‘Arafāt and thinks that Allah will not forgive him—may Allah not forgive him.”

And also:

“If a shepherd were to pass through ‘Arafāt—without knowing that it was the Day of ‘Arafah—he would be forgiven.”

And the saying attributed to him, peace be upon him:

“Whoever performs Hajj but does not visit me has slighted me, and whoever visits me will be entitled to my intercession.”

Are these hadiths found in the Sahīh collections or not? And what is the meaning of His words, Mighty and Majestic:

“The standing place of Abraham; whoever enters it shall be safe”?

He answered:

Praise be to Allah, Lord of all worlds. None of these hadiths appears in either the Sahīh or the Sunan collections. Some of them convey meanings contrary to the Quran and Sunnah. If a man were to stand at ‘Arafāt fearing that Allah might not forgive his sins because they are major sins, it could not be said that Allah would not forgive him. Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, but He forgives whatever is less than that for whomever He wills. Thus, He may forgive a person’s sins that fall short of associating partners with Him if He wills, or He may withhold forgiveness if He wills. However, when a servant repents of a sin, Allah forgives it, whether it involves associating partners with Him or anything else.

As Allah Most High says:

“O My servants who have transgressed against

Moreover, standing at ‘Arafāt does not discharge a person’s obligations of prayer and zakat, by the consensus of the Muslims. Indeed, they agree that prayer is incomparably more binding than Hajj. Hajj is obligatory once in a lifetime for those able to undertake it, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed Hajj only once after the Hijrah. Prayer, by contrast, is obligatory upon every sane adult—except menstruating women and women experiencing postnatal bleeding—whether healthy or ill, safe or fearful, rich or poor, male or female. Over each day and night, there are some forty units of prayer: seventeen obligatory units, ten or twelve units of regular Sunnah prayers, and eleven or thirteen units of night prayer.

Likewise, people’s rights arising from sins, injustices and other matters are not discharged through Hajj, by the agreement of the imams. The report narrated from ‘Abbās ibn Mirdās concerning the discharge of injustices and other liabilities through Hajj is weak.

It is established in the Sahīh that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The five daily prayers, from one Friday prayer to the next, and from one Ramadan to the next, expiate the sins committed between them, provided that major sins are avoided.”

These observances are greater than Hajj. Major sins, however, are expiated by repentance from them, according to the Quran, the Sunnah and the consensus of the Muslim community.

Likewise, the saying attributed to him,

“Whoever performs Hajj but does not visit me has slighted me,”

is a fabrication. Slighting the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is forbidden, whereas visiting his grave is not obligatory, by the agreement of the Muslims. No authentic hadith from him concerning visiting his grave has been established. Indeed, reports such as “Whoever visits me and my father in a single year, I guarantee him Paradise from Allah,” and others like it, are fabrications by the agreement of the scholars. Al-Dāraqutnī and others narrated hadiths concerning visiting his grave, but they are weak.

Imam Mālik—who was among those most knowledgeable about the rights of Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the Sunnah followed by the inhabitants of his city among the Companions, the Successors and their successors—disapproved of saying, “I visited the grave of Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” Had this wording been authentically established from Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and known to the scholars of Madinah, Mālik would not have disapproved of it.

As for saying, “I greeted Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace,” this is unobjectionable by agreement. As reported from him in the Sunan collections, he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“No man greets me with peace but Allah restores my soul to me so that I may return his greeting.”

Ibn ‘Umar used to say: “Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. Peace be upon you, O Abū Bakr. Peace be upon you, my father.”

In Sunan Abī Dāwūd, he is reported to have said:

“Send abundant blessings upon me on Friday and the night before it, for your blessings are presented to me.” They asked, “How will our blessings be presented to you when you have decayed?” He replied, “Allah has indeed forbidden

the earth to consume the flesh of the prophets.”

As for His words, Exalted is He,

“Whoever enters it is safe,”

this concerns the Sacred House. As He, Exalted is He, says:

“Have they not seen that We have made a secure sanctuary, while people are snatched away all around them?”

And He, Exalted is He, says:

“Let them worship the Lord of this House, who has fed them against hunger and secured them against fear.”

And He, Exalted is He, says:

“Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary to which fruits of every kind are brought?”

During the days of pre-Islamic ignorance, they would kill one another outside the Sanctuary. But when they entered the Sanctuary, even a man who encountered his father’s killer would leave him unharmed. This was among the signs Allah placed within it, as He says:

“In it are clear signs, including the standing place of Abraham. Whoever enters it is safe.”

Islam further increased its sanctity. Thus, the position of most jurists is that someone who commits an offence punishable by a prescribed penalty outside the Sanctuary and then takes refuge within it is not subjected to that penalty until he leaves. This was the view expressed by Ibn ‘Umar and Ibn ‘Abbās, and it is the position of Abū Hanīfah, Ahmad and others. For it is authentically established in the Sahīh that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Allah made Makkah sacred; it was not people who made it sacred. It is therefore not lawful for anyone who believes in Allah and the Last Day to shed blood or cut down trees there. Its inviolability was not suspended for anyone before me, nor will it be suspended for anyone after me. It was suspended for me only for an hour of one day, and today its sanctity has returned to what it was yesterday.”

translated_text:
He—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked about the following hadith:

“If someone teaches you a verse from the Book of Allah, it is as though he owns you as a slave: he may sell you if he wishes or set you free if he wishes.”

Is this found in the Six Books, or is it a lie attributed to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?

He replied:

This is not found in any of the Muslims’ books, neither the Six Books nor any others. Rather, it contradicts the consensus of the Muslims. Teaching someone does not make the teacher that person’s owner, entitled to sell him or set him free as he wishes. Anyone who believes this is to be called upon to repent; if he repents, well and good; otherwise, he is to be put to death. A free Muslim cannot be enslaved.

The foremost teacher of mankind, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, taught them the Book and wisdom, and he has a greater claim over them than they have over themselves. Nevertheless, they remained free: he neither enslaved them nor made them his servants in bondage. Rather, the rulings governing his relations with the free members of his community differed from those governing his relations with the slaves he owned. Had the believing women been his property, he would have been permitted to have intercourse with any believing woman without a marriage contract. Likewise, anyone who taught a woman a verse of the Quran would have been entitled to have intercourse with her without marriage. No Muslim would say this.

He was asked about the meaning of the Prophet’s saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“Whoever rebukes an adherent of religious innovation, Allah will fill his heart with security and faith and grant him safety on the Day of the Greatest Terror.”

He replied:

As for the sayings, “Whoever rebukes an adherent of religious innovation, Allah will fill his heart with security and faith,” and “Whoever honors an adherent of religious innovation helps to destroy Islam,” and similar statements, these words are known to have been said by al-Fudayl ibn ‘Iyād.

Religious innovation consists of beliefs and acts of worship that contradict the Book and the Sunnah or the consensus of the early generations of the Muslim community. Examples include the doctrines of the Khawārij, Rāfidah, Qadariyyah and Jahmiyyah; the practices of those who worship through dancing and singing in mosques, or through shaving their beards and consuming hashish; and similar innovations adopted as acts of worship by groups that oppose the Book and the Sunnah. And Allah knows best.

translated_text:
He was asked about someone who heard a man say:

“If you had done such and such, none of this would have happened to you.”

Another man who heard him said, “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade this expression. It is an expression that leads the one who utters it to disbelief.”

A third man said, “Regarding the story of Moses and al-Khidr, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

‘May Allah have mercy on Moses. We wish he had been patient, so that Allah might have told us more of their story.’”

The other man cited the Prophet’s saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer”—until he said—“for the word ‘if’ opens the way for Satan’s work.”

Does one of these abrogate the other, or not?

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. Everything Allah and His Messenger have said is true. The word “if” is used in two ways:

(The first is to express grief over the past and distress at what has been decreed. This is what he forbade, as Allah Most High says:

“O you who believe, do not be

like those who disbelieved and said of their brothers who travelled through the land or went out to battle, ‘Had they stayed with us, they would not have died or been killed,’ so that Allah may make this a source of regret in their hearts.” This is what the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade when he said:

“If something befalls you, do not say, ‘If only I had done such and such, this and that would have happened.’ Rather, say, ‘Allah decreed it, and He does whatever He wills,’ for ‘if’ opens the way for Satan’s work.”

That is, it opens the way for grief and distress, which harm you and bring no benefit. Rather, know that whatever befell you could never have missed you, and whatever missed you could never have befallen you. As Allah Most High says:

“No calamity befalls except by Allah’s permission. And whoever believes in Allah, He guides his heart.”

They explained: this is the man who suffers a calamity and knows that it is from Allah, so he is content and submits.

(The second use of “if” is to convey beneficial knowledge, as in the words of Allah Most High:

“Had there been gods besides Allah in the heavens and the earth, both would have fallen into ruin.”

It may also express love of good and the desire to do it, as in the saying, “If I had wealth like so-and-so, I would do as he does.” This and similar expressions are permissible. The Prophet’s saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace,

“I wish Moses had been patient, so that Allah might have told us more of their story,”

belongs to this category, as does His saying:

“They wish you would compromise, so that they too would compromise.”

Our Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wished that Allah would recount their story. He therefore mentioned them both to express his love for the patience on which that depended, thereby making known what would have happened, because of the benefit in that. translated_text:
He was asked:

“Regarding the account of Iblīs speaking to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was in the mosque with a group of his Companions, and the Prophet questioning him about many matters while the people plainly saw his form and heard him speaking aloud: is this an authentic hadith or a fabricated lie? Does it appear in any of the Sahīh, Musnad, or Sunan collections? Is it permissible for anyone to narrate it? What should be done about someone who narrates it to people and claims that it is authentic and religiously authoritative?”

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. Rather, this is a fabricated lie. It is not found in any of the Muslims’ authoritative hadith collections—neither the Sahīh collections, nor the Sunan collections, nor the Musnad collections.

Anyone who knows that it is a lie attributed to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is not permitted to narrate it from him. Anyone who claims that it is authentic is to be informed of its true status; if he persists, he is to be punished for that.

However, it contains much material compiled from prophetic hadiths. The person who fabricated and invented it assembled it from reports, some false and some true. This is why it contains several authentic statements, even though the underlying account—Iblīs appearing visibly before the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the presence of his Companions, and the Prophet questioning him—is a fabricated lie that none of the Muslim scholars has transmitted. And Allah, glorified and exalted is He, knows best.

translated_text:
He also said—may Allah Most High have mercy on him:

The book Tanaqqulāt al-Anwār (The Passage of the Lights), attributed to Ahmad ibn ‘Abd Allāh al-Bakrī, is among the books most filled with lies and fabrications against Allah, His Messenger, and the Companions of Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Its author has invented accounts like those fabricated in the tales of Dalhama and al-Battāl, the tales of ‘Antara, the stories of al-Rashīd and his vizier Ja‘far al-Barmakī, and the stories of adventurers such as al-Zi’baq the Egyptian and Ahmad al-Danq, and other such works.

But those writers fabricate lies about people who are not prophets, whereas the author of the book he called Tanaqqulāt al-Anwār fabricates lies about Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his Companions. He attributes to him lies the like of which no one is known to have written in any book. Even if some of what he relates contains a very little truth, it is of the same kind as that found in the tales of ‘Antara and al-Battāl. ‘Antara was indeed a poet and one of the horsemen of the pre-Islamic era. His poetry is well known, and one of his odes is among the seven Mu‘allaqāt (Suspended Odes). Yet they fabricated more lies about him than anyone but Allah can count, and each successive storyteller added further falsehoods to those tales.

translated_text:
Likewise, Abū Muhammad al-Battāl was a well-known Muslim commander. The Muslims had undertaken two expeditions against Constantinople.

The first was during the caliphate of Mu‘āwiya, who placed his son Yazīd in command. Abū Ayyūb al-Ansārī accompanied him—the Companion in whose house the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stayed when he emigrated to Medina. Abū Ayyūb died during that expedition and was buried near Constantinople. Al-Bukhārī narrated in his Sahīh, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The first army to campaign against Constantinople will be forgiven.”

The second expedition was during the caliphate of ‘Abd al-Malik ibn Marwān. He placed his son Maslama in command—or left his son al-Walīd in his place—and sent a vast army with him. They besieged the city and remained there for several years. They then concluded a peace agreement with its people allowing them to enter it, and built a mosque there. That mosque remains to this day.

Then the liars came and added to the tales of al-Battāl and ‘Abd al-Wahhāb more falsehoods than anyone but Allah can count. These accounts mentioned Dalhama, the judge ‘Aqibah, and things with no basis in reality.

Al-Bakrī, the author of Tanaqqulāt al-Anwār (The Passage of the Lights), followed the path of these lying fabricators. Yet his lies about Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his Companions—the finest of creation after the prophets—are even more numerous. His book contains kinds of fabricated falsehoods and outlandish inventions that defy description, such as the tale of the Seven Fortresses

وَهَضَّامِ بْنِ جِحَافٍ وَمِثْلَ حَدِيثِ الدَّهْرِ وَرَأْسِ الْغُولِ وكلندجة وَغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِنْ كُتُبِهِ وَغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِنْ ذِكْرِ أَمَاكِنَ لَا وُجُودَ لَهَا وَغَزَوَاتٍ لَا حَقِيقَةَ لَهَا وَأَسْمَاءٍ وَمُسَمَّيَاتٍ لَا يَعْرِفُهَا أَحَدٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ وَرِوَايَةِ أَحَادِيثَ تُخَالِفُ كِتَابَ اللَّهِ وَسُنَّةَ رَسُولِهِ وَإِجْمَاعَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَتُخَالِفُ مَا تَوَاتَرَ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ. وَفِيهَا مِنْ الْأَقْوَالِ وَالْأَفْعَالِ الْمُضَافَةِ إلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَأَصْحَابِهِ مَا بَرَّأَهُ اللَّهُ مِنْهُ وَهِيَ مِنْ جِنْسِ أَحَادِيثِ الزَّنَادِقَةِ الْنُصَيْرِيَّة وَأَشْبَاهِهِمْ الَّذِينَ يَخْتَلِقُونَ مَا فِيهِ غُلُوٌّ فِي عَلِيٍّ وَغَيْرِهِ وَفِيهِ مِنْ الْقَدْحِ فِي دِينِ الْإِسْلَامِ وَالْإِفْسَادِ لَهُ مَا يُوجِبُ إبَاحَةَ دَمِ مَنْ يَقُولُ ذَلِكَ وَإِنْ كَانَ جَاهِلًا اُسْتُتِيبَ فَإِنْ تَابَ وَإِلَّا قُتِلَ. وَأَقَلُّ مَا يُفْعَلُ بِمَنْ يَرْوِي مِثْلَ هَذَا أَنْ يُعَاقَبَ عُقُوبَةً تَرْدَعُهُ عَنْ مِثْلِ ذَلِكَ وَكَذَلِكَ يَسْتَحِقُّ الْعُقُوبَةَ مَنْ يُكْرِيهَا لِمَنْ يَقْرَؤُهَا وَيُصَدِّقُ مَا فِيهَا وَمَنْ يَنْسَخُهَا أَيْضًا كَذَلِكَ.
 وَيَجِبُ عَلَى أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ إظْهَارُ مَا يَعْلَمُونَ مِنْ كَذِبِ هَذِهِ وَأَمْثَالِهَا فَكَمَا يَجِبُ بَيَانُ كَذِبِ مَا نُقِلَ عَنْهُ فِي الْأَحَادِيثِ كَأَحَادِيثِ الْبُخَارِيِّ:
 يَجِبُ بَيَانُ كَذِبِ مَا كَذَبَ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ الْأَحَادِيثِ الْمَوْضُوعَةِ الَّتِي يَعْلَمُ أَنَّهَا كَذِبٌ كَمَا بَيَّنَ أَهْلُ الْعِلْمِ مِنْ حَالِ مَنْ كَانَ يَكْذِبُ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ الرُّوَاةِ
translated_text:
and Haddām ibn Jihāf, and tales such as Time, The Ghoul’s Head, Kalindaja, and other works of his. These mention places that do not exist, campaigns that never occurred, and names and entities unknown to any scholar. They transmit reports that contradict Allah’s Book, His Messenger’s Sunnah, the consensus of the Muslims, and what has been transmitted through numerous independent chains from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

They attribute to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his Companions words and deeds of which Allah has declared him innocent. These resemble the reports of the Nusayrī heretics and their like, who fabricate accounts involving excessive veneration of ‘Alī and others. They contain attacks upon Islam and corruption of it that warrant putting those who utter such things to death. If such a person is ignorant, he must be called upon to repent; if he repents, he is spared, but otherwise he is executed. The least that should be done to anyone who narrates such material is to punish him sufficiently to deter him from doing so again. Likewise, anyone who rents these books to someone who reads them and believes their contents deserves punishment, as does anyone who copies them.

Scholars must expose the falsehood they recognize in these works and others like them. For just as it is obligatory to expose the falsehood of what has been transmitted from him in hadiths such as those of al-Bukhārī, it is obligatory to expose the falsehood of the fabricated hadiths falsely attributed to him that are known to be lies, just as scholars have explained the circumstances of those narrators who lied about him

original_text:
وَبَيَانِ مَا نُقِلَ عَنْهُ مِنْ الْكَذِبِ الَّذِي يَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ كَذِبٌ وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْ الْمَوْضُوعَاتِ إنَّمَا يَعْلَمُ أَنَّهَا مَوْضُوعَةٌ خَوَاصُّ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ بِالْأَحَادِيثِ وَأَمَّا مِثْلُ مَا فِي 
" تَنَقُّلَاتِ الْأَنْوَارِ "
 مِنْ الْأَحَادِيثِ فَهُوَ مِمَّا يَعْلَمُهُ مَنْ لَهُ أَدْنَى عِلْمٍ بِأَحْوَالِ الرَّسُولِ وَمَغَازِيهِ أَنَّهُ كَذِبٌ. وَعَلَى وُلَاةِ الْأُمُورِ عُقُوبَةُ مَنْ يَرْوِي هَذِهِ أَوْ يُعِينُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ بِنَوْعِ مِنْ أَنْوَاعِ الْإِعَانَةِ وَلِوَلِيِّ الْأَمْرِ أَنْ يُحْرِقَهَا فَقَدْ حَرَقَ عُثْمَانُ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ كُتُبًا هَذِهِ أَوْلَى بِالتَّحْرِيقِ مِنْهَا وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
translated_text:
and exposed the false reports attributed to him that they know to be lies. Many fabricated reports are recognized as such only by specialists in hadith. As for reports such as those found in *Tanaqqulāt al-Anwār*, anyone with even the slightest knowledge of the Messenger’s life and military campaigns knows that they are false.

The authorities must punish anyone who narrates these reports or assists in doing so in any way. The ruler may burn these books, for ‘Uthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, burned books, and these are more deserving of being burned than those were. And Allah knows best.

original_text:
مَا تَقُولُهُ السَّادَةُ الْعُلَمَاءُ - رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ -
 أَجْمَعِينَ:
فِي أُنَاسٍ قَصَّاصِينَ؟ يَنْقُلُونَ مَغَازِيَ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَقَصَصَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ - عَلَيْهِمْ السَّلَامُ -
 تَحْتَ الْقَلْعَةِ وَفِي الْجَوَامِعِ وَالْأَسْوَاقِ وَيَقُولُونَ:
 إنَّ النَّبِيَّ أَتَى إلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ يُقَالُ لَهُ: حَبِيبٌ فَقَالَ لَهُ: إنْ كُنْت رَسُولَ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّا نُرِيدُ أَنَّ الْقَمَرَ لَيْلَةَ تِسْعٍ وَعِشْرِينَ يَعُودُ وَيَنْزِلُ مِنْ طَوْقِك وَيَطْلُعُ مِنْ أَكْمَامِك فَأَرَاهُمْ ذَلِكَ فَآمَنُوا بِهِ جَمِيعُهُمْ وَقَالَ: كَانُوا الرَّبَّ.
 وَيَقُولُونَ:
 إنَّهُ أَتَى إلَيْهِ مَلِكٌ يُقَالُ لَهُ: بَشِيرُ بْنُ غَنَّامٍ عَمِلَ عَلَيْهِ حِيلَةً وَأَخَذَ مِنْهُ تِسْعَ أَنْفُسٍ عَلَّقَهُمْ عَلَى النَّخْلِ فَبَعَثَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَلِيًّا فَخَلَّصَهُمْ وَكَانَ مِنْ جُمْلَتِهِمْ خَالِدٌ.
 وَأَتَى إلَيْهِ مَلِكٌ وَهُوَ فِي مَكَّةَ يُقَالُ لَهُ:
 الْمَلِكُ الدِّحَاقُ وَكَانَتْ لَهُ بِنْتٌ اسْمُهَا حمانة فَكَسَرَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَزَوْجُ بِنْتِهِ لِبِلَالِ فَقَتَلَهُ وَهُوَ فِي الصَّلَاةِ فَحَطَّ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بُرْدَتَهُ فَأَحْيَاهُ اللَّهُ لَهُ.
translated_text:
What do the esteemed scholars—may Allah be pleased with them all—say concerning storytellers who recount the Prophet’s military campaigns, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the stories of the prophets, peace be upon them, below the citadel, in congregational mosques and in marketplaces? They say:

An angel named Habīb came to the Prophet and said to him, “If you are Allah’s Messenger, we want the moon, on the twenty-ninth night, to return, descend through your collar and emerge from your sleeves.” He showed them this, and they all believed in him. He said, “They were the Lord.”

They also say that a king named Bashīr ibn Ghannām came to him, tricked him and seized nine people from him, whom he hung on palm trees. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent ‘Alī, who rescued them. Khālid was among them.

A king called al-Dihāq came to him while he was in Mecca. He had a daughter named Hamānah. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then broke [him] and married his daughter to Bilāl. He then killed him while he was praying. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, laid down his cloak, and Allah restored him to life for him.

original_text:
وَأَنَّهُ بُعِثَ الْمِقْدَادُ إلَى مَلِكٍ يُقَالُ لَهُ:
 الْمَلِكُ الْخَطَّارُ فَالْتَقَى فِي طَرِيقِهِ مَلِكَةً يُقَالُ لَهَا: رَوْضَةَ فَتَزَوَّجَ بِهَا وَرَاحَ إلَى الْمَلِكِ الَّذِي أُرْسِلَ إلَيْهِ فَاقْتَتَلَ هُوَ وَإِيَّاهُ فَأَسَرَهُ وَجَاءَ إلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَقَاتَلَ فِي غُزَاةِ تَبُوكَ بولص بْنُ عَبْدِ الصَّلِيبِ وَأَنَّهُ قَاتَلَ فِي الْأَحْزَابِ وَكَانُوا أُلُوفًا وَانْكَسَرَتْ الْأَحْزَابُ قُدَّامَ عَلِيٍّ سَبْعَ عَشْرَةَ فِرْقَةً وَخَلْفَ كُلِّ وَاحِدَةٍ رَجُلٌ يَضْرِبُ بِالسَّيْفِ وَيَقُولُ: أَنَا عَلِيٌّ - وَلِيُّهُ -
 ضَرَبَ عَمْرَو بْنَ الْعَامِرِيِّ فَقَطَعَ فَخْذَهُ فَأَخَذَ عَمْرٌو فَخِذَهُ وَضَرَبَ بِهَا فِي الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَقَلَعَ شَجَرَةً وَقَتَلَ بِهَا جَمَاعَةً مِنْهُمْ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ ضَجَّتْ عِنْدَ ذَلِكَ وَقَالُوا:
 لَا سَيْفَ إلَّا ذُو الْفَقَارِ وَلَا فَتَى إلَّا عَلِيٌّ.
 وَأَنَّ عَلِيًّا قَاتَلَ الْجِنَّ فِي الْبِئْرِ وَرَمَاهُ بِالْمَنْجَنِيقِ إلَى حِصْنِ الْغُرَابِ وَجَاءَتْ رَمْيَتُهُ نَاقِصَةً فَمَشَى فِي الْهَوَاءِ وَأَنَّهُ ضَرَبَ مَرْحَبًا الْيَهُودِيَّ وَكَانَ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ جُرْنٌ رُخَامٌ فَقُسِمَ لَهُ وَلِلْفَرَسِ نِصْفَيْنِ وَأَنَّهُ عَبَرَ الْعَسْكَرُ عَلَى زَنْدِهِ إلَى خَيْبَرَ وَهَدَّ الْحِصْنَ وَأَنَّ ذُو الْفَقَارِ أُنْزِلَ إلَيْهِ مِنْ السَّمَاءِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمَّاهُ مِنْ السَّمَاءِ وَقَالَ:
 عَلِيٌّ أَسْبَقُ مِنْ الْعَجَلِ وَأَنَّهُ بُعِثَ مَعَ كُلِّ نَبِيٍّ سِرًّا وَبُعِثَ مَعَ النَّبِيِّ جَهْرًا وَأَنَّهُ كَانَ عَصَا مُوسَى وَسَفِينَةَ نُوحٍ وَخَاتَمَ سُلَيْمَانَ وَأَنَّهُ شَرِبَ مِنْ سُرَّةِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لَمَّا مَاتَ فَوَزَنَ عِلْمَ الْأَوَّلِينَ والآخرين. وَأَنَّ مَلَكَ الْمَوْتِ جَاءَ إلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي زِيِّ أَعْرَابِيٍّ
translated_text:
and that al-Miqdād was sent to a king called al-Malik al-Khattār. On his way, he met a queen named Rawdah and married her. He then went to the king to whom he had been sent, fought him, took him captive and came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Būlus ibn ‘Abd al-Salīb fought in the expedition of Tabūk.

And that he fought at the Battle of the Confederates, when they numbered thousands. The Confederates broke before ‘Alī into seventeen divisions, behind each of which stood a man striking with a sword and saying, “I am ‘Alī—his ally.” He struck ‘Amr ibn al-‘Āmirī and severed his thigh. ‘Amr took his thigh and struck the Muslims with it, then uprooted a tree and killed a number of them with it. At that, the angels cried out, saying:

“There is no sword but Dhū al-Fiqār,
and no valiant warrior but ‘Alī.”

And that ‘Alī fought the jinn in the well and was launched by catapult towards the fortress of al-Ghurāb. His flight fell short, so he walked through the air. And that he struck Marhab the Jew, who had a marble basin on his head, splitting both him and his horse in two. And that the army crossed over his forearm to Khaybar, and he demolished the fortress. And that Dhū al-Fiqār was sent down to him from heaven, for Allah named him from heaven and said, “‘Alī is swifter than haste.”

And that he was sent secretly with every prophet, but openly with the Prophet; that he was Moses’ staff, Noah’s ark and Solomon’s ring; and that he drank from the Prophet’s navel, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when he died, and weighed the knowledge of the first and the last.

And that the Angel of Death came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the guise of a Bedouin

original_text:
فَقَالَ لَهُ النَّبِيُّ:
 قَابِضٌ أَمْ زَائِرٌ؟
 فَقَالَ لَهُ:
 مَا زُرْت أَحَدًا مِنْ قَبْلِك حَتَّى أَزُورَك فَأَعْطَاهُ تُفَّاحَةً فَشَمَّهَا فَخَرَجَتْ رُوحُهُ فِيهَا وَأَنَّ فَاطِمَةَ بَكَتْ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى أَقْلَقَتْ أَهْلَ الْمَدِينَةِ حَتَّى أَخْرَجُوهَا إلَى بُيُوتِ الْأَحْزَانِ وَيَنْقُلُونَ قَصَصَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ مِنْ جِنْسِ هَذَا السُّؤَالِ وَيُفَسِّرُونَهَا بِآيَاتِ لَمْ تُسْمَعْ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ وَكُلُّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْ هَذِهِ تَحَزَّبُوا فِيهَا لَيْلَةً.
 وَكَانَ بَعْضُ الْعُلَمَاءِ قَدْ مَنَعَهُمْ مِنْ هَذَا النَّقْلِ وَأَنَّهُمْ لَا يَنْقُلُونَ إلَّا مَنْ كَتَبَ عَلَيْهَا سَمَّاعَاتِ الْمَشَايِخِ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ فَاعْتَمَدُوا عَلَى كُتُبٍ فِيهَا مِنْ جِنْسِ مَا ذُكِرَ مِنْ تَصْنِيفِ رَجُلٍ يُقَالُ لَهُ:
 الْبَكْرِيُّ فَمَا يَجِبُ عَلَيْهِمْ فِي مِثْلِ هَذِهِ الْأُمُورِ؟ لِأَنَّهُمْ يَنْقُلُونَ مَا يُخَالِفُ مَا ثَبَتَ عَنْ الرُّسُلِ عَلَيْهِمْ السَّلَامُ وَيَنْقُلُونَ فِي بَعْضِ الْأَشْيَاءِ مَا هُوَ تَنْقِيصٌ بِهِمْ وَهَلْ يُثَابُ مَنْ أَمَرَ بِمَنْعِهِمْ.
 وَيَنْقُلُونَ أَيْضًا:
 أَنَّ اللَّهَ قَبَضَ مِنْ نُورِ وَجْهِهِ قَبْضَةً وَنَظَرَ إلَيْهَا فَعَرِقَتْ وَدَلَقَتْ فَخَلَقَ اللَّهُ مِنْ كُلِّ قَطْرَةٍ نَبِيًّا وَكَانَتْ الْقَبْضَةُ النَّبِيَّ وَبَقِيَ كَوْكَبٌ دُرِّيٌّ وَكَانَ نُورًا مَنْقُولًا مِنْ أَصْلَابِ الرِّجَالِ إلَى بُطُونِ النِّسَاءِ.
فَأَجَابَ شَيْخُ الْإِسْلَامِ قُدْوَةُ الْإِيمَانِ تَقِيُّ الدِّينِ أَبُو الْعَبَّاسِ أَحْمَد بْنُ عَبْدِ الْحَلِيمِ بْنِ عَبْدِ السَّلَامِ ابْنُ تَيْمِيَّة الْحَرَّانِي فَقَالَ:
translated_text:
and the Prophet said to him, “Have you come to take my soul or to visit?” He replied, “I have never visited anyone before you, that I should visit you.” He then gave him an apple, which he smelled, and his soul departed into it. And that Fātimah wept over him until she disturbed the people of Medina, who took her out to the houses of mourning. They also recount stories about the prophets like those mentioned in this question, explaining them through verses never heard from the scholars. They gather together for a night over each of these accounts.

Some scholars had forbidden them to transmit such material, requiring them to transmit only material bearing records of readings before learned shaykhs. They therefore relied on books containing accounts like those mentioned above, composed by a man called al-Bakrī. What, then, must they do concerning such matters? For they transmit things that contradict what is reliably reported from the messengers, peace be upon them, and some of what they transmit disparages them. Will someone who orders that they be stopped be rewarded?

They also relate that Allah took a handful of the light of His Face and looked at it, whereupon it sweated and shed drops. Allah created a prophet from every drop. That handful was the Prophet, and a brilliant star remained; it was a light passed from the loins of men to the wombs of women.

Shaykh al-Islām, the exemplar of faith, Taqī al-Dīn Abū al-‘Abbās Ahmad ibn ‘Abd al-Halīm ibn ‘Abd al-Salām Ibn Taymiyyah al-Harrānī, answered, saying:

original_text:
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ، هَذِهِ الْأَحَادِيثُ مِنْ الْأَحَادِيثِ الْمُفْتَرَاةِ بِاتِّفَاقِ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ وَإِنَّمَا تُؤْخَذُ مِثْلُ هَذِهِ الْأَحَادِيثِ مِنْ مِثْلِ

 فِرْقَةً دُونَ الْجَبَلِ وَفِرْقَةً فَوْقَ الْجَبَلِ. وَكَذَلِكَ حَبِيبُ أَبِي مَالِكٍ لَا وُجُودَ لَهُ وَالْحَدِيثُ الْمَذْكُورُ عَنْ بَشِيرِ بْنِ غَنَّامٍ أَيْضًا كَذِبٌ وَهَذَا الِاسْمُ غَيْرُ مَعْرُوفٍ. وَخَالِدُ بْنُ الْوَلِيدِ لَمْ يُؤْسَرْ أَصْلًا بَلْ أَسْلَمَ بَعْدَ الْحُدَيْبِيَةِ وَمَا زَالَ مَنْصُورًا فِي حُرُوبِهِ. وَكَذَلِكَ مَا ذُكِرَ عَنْ الْمُسَمَّى بِالْمَلِكِ الدِّحَاقِ كَذِبٌ وَهَذَا الِاسْمُ لَا وُجُودَ لَهُ فِيمَنْ حَارَبَهُ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَاشَ وَلَكِنْ الَّذِينَ عَاشُوا بَعْدَ الْمَوْتِ فِي هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ كَانَ بَيْنَهُمْ طَائِفَةٌ فِي زَمَنِ الصَّحَابَةِ وَالتَّابِعِينَ وَأَمَّا مَنْ أَحْيَا اللَّهَ لَهُ دَابَّتَهُ بَعْدَ الْمَوْتَ مِنْ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فَهَؤُلَاءِ بَعْضُهُمْ كَانَ مِنْ الْمُسْلِمِينَ عَلَى عَهْدِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ كَانَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ.
translated_text:
Praise be to Allah, Lord of all worlds. These reports are fabrications by the consensus of the scholars. Such reports are drawn only from works like al-Bakrī’s Tanaqqulāt al-anwār (The Passage of the Lights), and from others like him who transmitted numerous lies.

As for the first account, the moon did not enter the neck opening of the Prophet’s clothing, peace and blessings be upon him, nor his garments, nor did it touch him. Rather, it split into two parts: one below the mountain and the other above it. Likewise, Habīb Abī Mālik never existed. The report mentioned about Bashīr ibn Ghannām is also a lie, and this name is unknown. Khālid ibn al-Walīd was never taken captive at all. Rather, he embraced Islam after al-Hudaybiyyah and remained victorious in his battles.

Likewise, what is related about the so-called King al-Dihāq is a lie. No one bearing this name was among those whom the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, fought. [He] lived; however, among those in this community who lived after death, there was a group in the time of the Companions and their Successors. As for the believers whose mounts Allah restored to life after death, some were Muslims during the lifetime of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, while others lived after his death, peace and blessings be upon him.

 وَكَذَلِكَ مَا ذُكِرَ مِنْ مُنَادَاةِ الْمُنَادِي بِقَوْلِهِ:
 " لَا سَيْفَ إلَّا ذُو
translated_text:
Likewise, what is related about the king named al-Khitār is a fabrication; no such person existed. As for the expedition to Tabūk, no fighting took place there. Rather, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, advanced towards the Byzantines, Arabs, and others in Syria. Never did more Muslims gather for an expedition with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, than gathered with him in the year of Tabūk, which was his last military expedition. He stayed at Tabūk for twenty days, but the Christians did not come out to confront him.

Likewise, during the campaign of the Confederates, there was no battle between the two armies. Rather, the Confederates besieged the Muslims from outside the trench that the Muslims had dug around Medina, while the Muslims remained inside it. There were a few skirmishes between some Muslims and some disbelievers, amounting to single combat or something similar. ʿAlī—may Allah be pleased with him—killed ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Wudd al-ʿĀmirī. The Confederates were not defeated through combat, nor were any significant numbers killed on either side. Rather, Allah sent against them the wind—the east wind—and sent the angels, as the Most High says in the account of the Confederates:

“O you who believe, remember Allah’s favor upon you when armies came against you, and We sent against them a wind and forces you did not see.”

And the following verses.

The account given of how ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Wudd al-ʿĀmirī was killed is a lie. Likewise, the claim that ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Wudd struck a tree with his thigh and uprooted it is a lie. There were no trees there; the date palms were far from the encampment.

Likewise, the account of a caller proclaiming:

“There is no sword but Dhū

translated_text:
al-Fiqār, and no hero but ʿAlī,” is a fabricated lie. Anyone who reports that this occurred on the day of Badr or on some other occasion is likewise lying. Dhū al-Fiqār was not ʿAlī’s sword; rather, it belonged to Abū Jahl, from whom the Muslims captured it as booty on the day of Badr. It was a sword made of metal. No sword descended from heaven, nor did this sword—or any other—grow longer.

Likewise, what he mentions about fighting the jinn—that ʿAlī or another human fought them in the well of Dhāt al-ʿIlm, or that some other human did so—is all lies. The jinn would never have fought the Companions in the first place. Rather, the disbelieving jinn used to fight the believing jinn. As for ʿAlī and his fellow Companions, their standing was far too great for the jinn to stand their ground against them in battle. It is established in the Sahīh that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb:

“Satan never sees you taking a path without taking a path other than yours.”

The account of ʿAlī being launched from a catapult and of the siege of the fortress called the Raven’s Fort is entirely a fabricated lie. The Muslims never launched anyone from a catapult towards the disbelievers—neither ʿAlī nor anyone else. Indeed, during the lifetime of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, the Muslims only ever set up a catapult against al-Tā’if, when the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, besieged it after the Battle of Hunayn and the defeat of Hawāzin. He besieged al-Tā’if, set up the catapult, and remained there for a month. It was not conquered until its people later embraced Islam voluntarily. And when

the Muslims were fighting Musaylimah the Liar and his followers, they drove them into their garden. The men then lifted al-Barā’ ibn Mālik and threw him over the wall into their midst, whereupon he opened the gate for them.

As for the account of Marhab, it is reported in the Sahīh that ‘Alī, may Allah be pleased with him, killed Marhab. It is also reported in the Sahīh that Muhammad ibn Maslamah killed Marhab. Some have said, “Rather, one of the two reports is mistaken.” As for the claim that the helmet on his head was a marble basin, that is a lie. Likewise, the claim that the blow split both the horseman and his horse and continued down into the ground—all of this is false. Scholars of the military campaigns and the Prophet’s biography have transmitted nothing of this kind; only ignorant people and liars relate it.

Even more obviously false is the account of the army crossing over ‘Alī’s forearm, the mule passing over it, and ‘Alī praying that it should have no offspring. Such stories are related only by people who are among the most ignorant of the Companions’ circumstances and of the realities of the world. Mules have always been sterile. There was no mule whatsoever in the army at Khaybar. Nor was there a mule with the Muslims, in Medina, or in the surrounding lands of Arabia, except the mule that al-Muqawqis, the ruler of Egypt, presented to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. He presented it to him after Khaybar; for when the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, concluded a peace agreement with the people of al-Hudaybiyah, he set out on his return journey
